edgeSemantics.after: technical producer interface prerequisites; never implicit whole-ticket completion
edgeSemantics.packageQualification: exact package discovery, source freeze, meaningful regression, canonical backend and fresh review
edgeSemantics.ticketClosure: Every mandatory original requirement needs accepted evidence or an explicit authorized scope decision. Mapping to remaining work, external blocker or downstream owner records an UNSATISFIED obligation, never completion.
edgeSemantics.release: required exact-SHA CI, trusted artifact and QA, exact-candidate recovery/final acceptance, separate release decision

stateSemantics.state: Implementation status ONLY: "complete", "partial", "open" or "not started". It never encodes dispatch readiness, blocking, priority or sequencing, and it never records acceptance, passing evidence or release eligibility.
stateSemantics.dispatchable: Ticket-level dispatch readiness, independent of state. false whenever any inbound consumedInputs checkpoint reads UNRESOLVED (see dispatchGates.inputReceipts), a named ticket-level blocking preflight is open (ADR-005 for 6.1, the original 18+3 map for 2.4, the grouped Places suite selection for 5.1), the ticket needs a coordinator-reserved shared edit or an exclusive qualification window that is not allocated (see dispatchGates.sourceFreeze and writerAllocation.coordinator.reservedFiles), or the ticket is complete and has no open writer package. dispatchGates.globalPreflights gates every dispatch on top of this field.
stateSemantics.separation: The two fields are independent and must stay so. A DELIVERED producer must never read as a blocker: its state records what is built and its consuming edges become verification items, as with 3.1 and CORE-REPLACE, where the prior conflation produced a false blocker on 11 edges. Conversely an unstarted ticket may be dispatchable, and a partially delivered ticket may not be. Neither field may be used to mark anything complete or passing.

dispatchGates.lifecycle: L0 observation/manual-review DTO and original 18+3 map
dispatchGates.music: exact backend/frontend/auth file allowlists, canonical principal handoff and socket qualification freeze. BLOCKING PREFLIGHT for every 6.1 package: docs/adr/005-music-identity-migration-deployment-authority.md is still Status Accepted and ratifies the bodyless POST /api/music/identity/ensure Strapi proof exchange that 6.1 must delete, so a writer following current ADR authority would rebuild exactly the boundary 6.1 exists to remove. ADR-005 must be superseded before any 6.1 writer is dispatched. ADR-006 is being drafted as Proposed by the architecture-authority owner and does not yet exist in docs/adr/ (001-005 plus README only).
dispatchGates.categories: typed core/media handoff plus CORE-REPLACE VERIFICATION when consumed; exact writer paths and guarded discovery. CORE-REPLACE is no longer a producer package: the producer is delivered and route-mounted (see the 3.1 inbound checkpoints), so a consuming package verifies the mounted route against the frozen runtime surface inventory and must not re-implement it. Its residual obligations are folded into 3.1 closure: the foreign-owner negative, the unchanged-other-creator negative, and UI adoption. No CORE-REPLACE producer package is dispatched.
dispatchGates.places: PLACES-CORE qualification selects only Places core owned scenarios and must NOT select the 5.2 place-links spec or the 5.4 claims spec, merely because a legacy suite alias groups them. The grouped Places suite selection is still present in the epic documents, which are owned by another document owner and are being corrected separately; until that lands, a PLACES-CORE run must use guarded exact discovery rather than the grouped alias, and 5.1 cannot qualify on the alias. All three tickets (5.1 core, 5.2 links, 5.4 claims) remain mandatory in full milestone discovery; no positive is removed, skipped or deferred to qualify core.
dispatchGates.shared: coordinator owns schema/routes/auth/Settings/migrations/seeds/manifests and the paths in writerAllocation.coordinator.reservedFiles; no writer may change any dependency inside the freeze roots while another package holds a protected qualification window (see dispatchGates.sourceFreeze)
dispatchGates.inputReceipts: Each producing package must write its exact reviewed receipt id back into every consuming edge checkpoint in this file at package close; that write-back is part of the producing package, not of the consumer. A consuming package whose inbound consumedInputs still read "UNRESOLVED" is NOT dispatchable, because the dispatchRequired item "reviewed input signatures/checkpoints" cannot be satisfied. Receipt ids are never fabricated, inferred or back-filled from a different freeze: an edge with no reviewed producer receipt stays UNRESOLVED and its consumer stays undispatchable. Current measured position, left as such deliberately rather than back-filled: 36 of the 77 consumedInputs entries still read UNRESOLVED, affecting 19 of the 38 tickets (3.5, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 9.1, 9.2, 10.1, 10.2, 10.3), every one of which is therefore undispatchable. The independent review's "19 of 38" is this ticket count, not an edge count.
dispatchGates.sourceFreeze: Repo-subtree-wide, never per-file. scripts/replatform-e2e.mjs snapshots whole subtrees (tunes/server, tunes/shared, tunes/auth-runtime, tunes/migrations, explorers-earth/src, explorers-earth/public, explorers-earth/e2e/replatform, explorers-earth/e2e/setup) and fails on any tracked-hash change OR any untracked or ignored file inside them, re-checking provenance before and during every lane (scripts/replatform-e2e.mjs:112,117,168,178). Consequence: implementation work on different tickets may overlap, but protected qualification takes an EXCLUSIVE repo-subtree window. No other writer may hold uncommitted, untracked or ignored files anywhere in those roots while a lane runs, so packages sharing a freeze domain cannot qualify in parallel even when their file allocations are disjoint. Every new file must be tracked before any lane runs, or the snapshot fails closed.
dispatchGates.globalPreflights: Cross-cutting preflights that gate EVERY dispatch regardless of a ticket's dispatchable value. Closed by this file: the CORE-REPLACE edge correction (11 inbound 3.1 checkpoints plus dispatchGates.categories), the coordinator reservation of the shared browser runner, suite manifest and browser fixtures, the repo-subtree-wide freeze statement, and the producer-receipt write-back rule. Still open and owned elsewhere: supersede ADR-005 with ADR-006 (blocks 6.1); produce the frozen original 18+3 lifecycle map (blocks 2.4); correct the grouped Places suite selection still carried by the epic documents (blocks 5.1 qualification); relabel the two "Create" lists that name existing files; and restate the three overstated counts (the 18-pass contained-route claim, "Games canonical 82", and the 12 lifecycle cases that exist only in the uncommitted overlay) while disclosing the 46ee hosted conclusions.

coordinator.reservedFilesRule: Coordinator-reserved and serialized: no category, lifecycle or Music writer may edit these, and no other document's ownership claim over the suite manifest applies. Every category and lifecycle package must change the runner, which is why it is reserved: scripts/replatform-e2e.mjs hardcodes the six lanes (auth, profile, books, lifecycle, movies, games) with exact per-lane identity counts, runners, configs and projects, enforces the forbidden-ambient-authority environment guard (assertEnvironment), and requires the manifest scopeContents and lane names to equal its own lane keys exactly, so a lane added, renamed or re-counted in the manifest alone fails validateManifest. The tunes/scripts/*-browser-fixture.ts entry points are named by the runner lane table and by its protected-target check. Adding or re-counting any browser lane is therefore a single serialized coordinator edit, requested with the exact lane name, runner, config, projects and identity count.
